paragraphs: Tick pose-change auto-fire, clear the per-update connected bit, cancel incompatible poses, then
dispatch GrappleBeam_Function through a synthetic near return. Every state returns with RTS to the
handler, which restores bank/status and exits long.
Set grapple liquid-physics flag bit 0 only for active pre-cancel states, without Gravity Suit,
with nonzero FX whose surface is above Samus's bottom boundary. All other states and environments
clear the bit after their state handler returns.
A new Shot edge from live or retained drawing input tail-enters grapple firing. Otherwise any
ordinary beam-charge/flare presentation is cleared and the suit palette restored, keeping inactive
grapple ownership separate from charge-beam visuals.
While Shot is held, extend by LengthDelta up to but not including 80h and test enemy collision
before block collision. A valid connection runs HandleConnectingGrapple, reverses LengthDelta to
signed -8 and publishes connected bit 0; release, maximum length or invalid collision cancels.
A locked connection persists only while Shot is held and either an enemy grapple result remains
nonzero or the endpoint is still attached to a grapple block. The retained connection returns carry
clear through the bank-$94 helper; a lost block or released input enters common cancellation.
Releasing Shot with zero angular velocity at angle 8000h drops without momentum. Every other release
converts swing angle/velocity into Samus motion, installs the released-from-swing grapple function
and gives movement ownership to SamusMovementHandler_ReleasedFromGrappleSwing.
Process D-pad length control, angular acceleration, velocity, kick and world movement in order.
Special-angle handling can finish the update early. Then revalidate enemy/block attachment, refresh
beam origin, report carry clear and synchronize Samus animation/position to the swing.
Holding Shot preserves a verified block attachment. Releasing Shot or losing the block starts a
thirty-update wall-jump opportunity and changes to WallGrabRelease; a retained grab reports carry
clear through the shared bank-$94 helper.
Pre-decrement the wall-jump window. Expiry drops Samus; while nonnegative, test a 16-pixel wall-jump
probe and switch to GrappleBeamFunction_WallJumping only when the shared collision helper returns
carry set.
Queue grapple-end sound, resolve the current grapple pose, clear beam/flare/timer state, restore the
equipped beam palette and default drawing, then run post-grapple collision correction. Auto-cancel
also clears the selected HUD item and its owner before returning to the inactive function.
Ordinary poses provide an eight-byte pose record containing Y offset and shot direction. A nonzero
direction high nibble means grapple cannot fire and enters common cancellation. Draygon-held poses
BE/F0 instead derive one of three facing-relative directions directly from held D-pad input.
Store the accepted direction, then load its X/Y extension subvelocity and initial endpoint angle.
Both angle copies start equal and a ten-update pose-change auto-fire timer keeps the launch active
across the immediate pose transition.
Moonwalking and non-running poses use the ordinary origin/flare tables; movement type one uses the
running tables. Subtract the pose Y offset before applying table Y values, and initialize beam start
and endpoint together while keeping the flare at its independent visual offset.
Clear endpoint offsets, swing/collision history and wall-jump state; start length at zero with delta
twelve and initialize segment animation. Grapple takes Samus drawing, installs the firing function,
loads beam palette two, queues sound five and cancels stale released-from-swing movement ownership.
Pose BE selects left-facing logic; the other held pose selects right-facing. A six-pixel Y origin
offset is shared, horizontal input gates diagonal tests, and the helper returns right/up-right/
down-right as 2/1/3 or left/up-left/down-left as 7/8/6, always with carry set.
Choose a safe post-grapple pose after a zero-momentum drop or missed wall jump. Swing poses B2/B3
map directly by rotation; otherwise Y radius selects standing/crouching direction tables, with
facing-based fallback when the current pose has no ordinary projectile direction.
Request the selected pose with command zero, publish solid vertical collision and clear all X/Y
speed. Then release grapple/flare/drawing ownership, restore palette and collision, consume any
auto-cancel HUD owner, and leave standing/crouching direction lookup tables inline.
Request wall-jump pose 83/84 from facing with command six, clear existing horizontal/vertical motion
and falling/collision state, then perform the same grapple/flare/palette/drawing teardown used by
other terminal states. The pose command supplies the actual wall-jump motion afterward.
Use angular-velocity magnitude and the sign-extended sine of the endpoint angle to produce 16.16
Samus Y speed. The sine sign selects down direction one or up direction two; negative and positive
angular velocity follow mirrored branches. Extra kick velocity is intentionally not included.
Select deceleration mode two, derive a velocity-dependent angular offset, sample the absolute sine
of the adjusted endpoint angle and multiply by angular magnitude. Store the 32-bit result as Samus
base X sub-speed/speed; the positive branch repeats the same transform at its nested label.
Angular-velocity sign selects released pose 51/52 and command seven while the movement handler keeps
the momentum calculated by PropelSamusFromGrappleSwing. Grapple, flare, palette and drawing state are
then retired without clearing the new Samus X/Y speed.
